title: How You Start... Shapes Everything
description: A practical prompt card built around the G.R.E.E.T framework — helping teachers design intentional, effective lesson openings that set the tone for student readiness and engagement.
tagline: Your lesson opening sets everything in motion.
origin: Grown from real PE lesson starts.
bestUsedWhen: A lesson needs a calmer, more intentional start
Students arrive distracted or dysregulated
You want routines to feel safe and predictable
You're reflecting on your own lesson opening habits
howItWorks: The G.R.E.E.T framework gives you five clear prompts for designing lesson openings that work — Greet, Routine, Engage, Explain, Transition. Use it as a planning checklist before the lesson or as a reflection tool after. It's designed to fit on one page so it stays useful, not theoretical.
reflectionPrompt: What small shift could make the beginning of this lesson feel safer, clearer, or more connected for your students?

title: Say Less... Get More
description: A prompt card built around the L.E.S.S framework — practical strategies for reducing teacher talk and increasing student thinking time in every lesson.
origin: Born from one too many lessons where I heard my own voice more than theirs.
bestUsedWhen: You notice students zoning out during instructions
You want to increase student agency and ownership
You're working on reducing unnecessary teacher talk
You want to create more space for student thinking
howItWorks: The L.E.S.S framework is a practical reminder card for in-lesson use. Limit your words. Engage before explaining. Signal, don't narrate. Step back and let them think. Each prompt is short enough to remember mid-lesson — the goal is to make silence feel purposeful rather than awkward.
reflectionPrompt: In your next lesson, count how many times you speak when a student could have instead. What did you notice?

title: Vertical & Horizontal Alignment
description: A visual guide using a garden metaphor to explain how vertical progression and horizontal alignment work together to create coherent, connected curriculum design.
origin: Created to explain curriculum coherence without the jargon.
bestUsedWhen: Planning across year groups or grade bands
Having curriculum conversations with your team
Reviewing whether your units connect meaningfully
Explaining curriculum design to newer teachers
howItWorks: The infographic maps vertical alignment (how skills and concepts deepen year on year) against horizontal alignment (how subjects and units connect within the same year). The garden metaphor — roots, trunk, branches — makes abstract curriculum theory visible and easy to discuss in a team meeting.
reflectionPrompt: Where does your curriculum have strong roots? Where are the branches growing in different directions?

title: Making Learning Visible
description: A practical infographic focusing on student ownership, assessment, reflection, and documentation — helping teachers make learning visible in meaningful ways.
tagline: When students see their learning, they own it.
origin: Grew from watching students genuinely surprise themselves.
bestUsedWhen: You want students to take more ownership of their learning
You're reviewing your approach to assessment and feedback
You want practical strategies, not just theory
You're exploring visible learning or assessment for learning
howItWorks: This infographic pulls together key strategies for making learning visible — through student reflection, documentation, peer feedback, and teacher observation. Each strategy is framed around what it looks like in practice, not just in theory. Print it, share it, stick it on your planning wall.
reflectionPrompt: What would your students say about their learning if you asked them right now? Would they be able to tell you what they're getting better at?

title: Teacher Communication Assistant
description: A Google Sheets template designed to support teachers with parent communication, professional correspondence, and navigating difficult conversations with clarity and confidence.
tagline: Say the right thing, the right way.
origin: Built after one too many late-night emails that needed a second pair of eyes.
bestUsedWhen: Writing a sensitive message to a parent or caregiver
Preparing for a difficult professional conversation
You want to sound confident, clear, and kind — at once
You're a newer teacher building communication confidence
howItWorks: Open the Google Sheet and make a copy to your own Drive. Choose from pre-written communication frameworks for common scenarios — parent updates, concern emails, positive feedback, meeting follow-ups — and adapt the language to your context. No login required beyond your Google account.
reflectionPrompt: What's one type of communication you find yourself putting off? Could a template take away enough friction to make it easier?

title: Class Compass
description: A gamified behaviour support tool for teachers and parents — grounded in Ross Greene, Daniel Siegel, Shanker, and Delahooke. Includes a Behaviour Translator, 18 strategies, 47 ready-to-use scripts, a 30-module course, and a Reflection Log.
tagline: Behaviour is information. Children do well when they can.
origin: Built because behaviour support shouldn't require a conference and a consultant.

title: PE Challenges
description: A student-facing web app for PE lessons — four challenge categories, progressive difficulty levels, video demos, score logging, and built-in reflection. Runs on any device, no login required.
tagline: Built for the gym, designed for engagement.

title: PE Circle
description: A teacher-facing app for opening and closing PE lessons with intention. Tracks student readiness, wellbeing, and ATL skills in real time. Password protected, syncs to Google Sheets.
tagline: Be more present with your students.

title: Team Quest
description: A team-based progression app where groups of 3–5 students level up together through physical and ATL collaboration challenges. IB/ATL aligned, grade-differentiated G1–G5, syncs to Google Sheets.
tagline: Building team culture, one challenge at a time.
